newsitem.title: USA: FBI appeals for release of two schoolgirls.
newsitem.headline: FBI appeals for release of two schoolgirls.

text.p: The FBI appealed Tuesday on national television for the abductors of two young sisters to "do the right thing," and release the girls while seeking to reassure the six and nine-year olds.

"To Ron Stafford and Rick Geer, do the right thing. Let's get these girls to a safe place, whether it is a police department, a school, a mission, anywhere they can be cared for," FBI agent Charles Goodwin said on NBC television's Today news programme.
"Then, let's get yourselves turned in and get this matter resolved," he said.

Addressing Teresa and Jessica Hainer, abducted Friday as they stepped off their schoolbus in Galesburg, Michigan, Goodwin said, "Their family loves them. Their community is very concerned about them."
The children may have been seen after midnight in the area around Gainesville, Florida, the same area where they were noticed at a car wash on Sunday.

FBI special agent Joseph Martinolich mentioned a sighting of the children six to eight hours before his 8 a.m. EST (1300 GMT) appearance on ABC television's Good Morning America but said he could not release details.
The two agents confirmed that law enforcement agencies were still concentrating their search in the Gainesville area but were also looking in other parts of the country.
The children have been the subject of a nationwide search by law enforcement since they got into a station wagon after school Friday with three men police believe were known to them.
Arrest warrants carrying charges of kidnapping were issued Saturday against Ronald Stafford, 21, his brother Lee Stafford, 17, and Ricky Geer, 19.

Teresa, 9, and Jessica, 6, were supposed to go to a baby sitter's home when they were dropped off in a trailer park in western Michigan, near Kalamazoo, but got into a cream-coloured 1988 Pontiac 6000 station wagon with wood-grain side panels and Michigan license plate number 1AX-J93.
FBI officials also appealed to citizens band radio operators to help in the search. They believe Ronald Stafford has a CB radio in the car and transmits under the handle name "Cookie Monster."
The FBI set up a telephone hotline number of 888-324-4969 for anyone with information on the girls' wherabouts.
